data: Binance USD-M futures; validation V1-V5 unchanged; flow normalized by each symbol's training median |flow|
forecast_calendar: train: 10th and 24th of each month 2023-2024; test: 6th and 20th, 2025-01 to 2026-09
guard_calendar: evaluation day = 15th; certification window = 12th-14th; train 2024; test 2025-01 to 2026-09
primary_1: thin: MAE_60 | C3_hat beyond CTRL + IMPACT + VOLBENCH (Part 9 specification), hour dummies, symbol fixed effects, re-estimated on these symbols' training days
primary_2: thin: MAE_60 | C3_hat beyond the same baseline plus VPIN (six-hour window, 50 equal-volume buckets, measured taker imbalance, winsorized at training 1%/99%)
primary_3: robust_guard vs static: q = min(1, k_s/(U_cert*S60_up)), S60_up = 90th percentile of 100 block-bootstrap refits of the certified T6 operator (Part 15 definitions); k_s = symbol training median; positions normalized to training mean 1; score log TLR difference
question: On Binance perpetuals never used in Parts 4-15: (1) does C3_hat forecast the next hour's adverse excursion beyond the Part 9 volatility baseline? (2) Does it still do so once VPIN is added to the baseline (confirming the post-hoc Part 13 R8 result)? (3) Does the uncertainty-aware guard of Part 15 lower tail loss per unit of position compared with a static limit at matched activity?
runs: X6 is run once; every run is counted in prereg/test_set_unlocks_p16.json
success: each primary passes if its Holm-adjusted one-sided p (across the three primaries) is below 0.05 and its 95% date-block bootstrap interval excludes zero in the predicted direction (dR2 > 0 for 1-2; log TLR difference < 0 for 3). p: Clark-West for 1-2; bootstrap share of draws >= 0 for 3
symbols: the 30 drawn in X2 (seeded, before analysis); thin = median training depth within 1% below $0.39M (Part 5 rule); only thin symbols enter the tests; at least 15 valid training and 15 valid test days required
